area.title: Overall dashboard home and at-a-glance drill-downs
area.scope: The service's home: the DR2.1 overall dashboard (category sections, glance cards and counts, Create new and Use template, messages), the prototype index, the at-a-glance drill-downs (action needed, status updated, inspection required) and today's INS front-door dashboard at / with its aggregated read model handoff and cross-service dashboards. Stops at a category's notification list (notification-list).

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. The prototype decides look and feel only (content, wording, layout, components, question order); it never decides architecture (sets, journeys, services, URL paths, field names, data-model shape, code structure). Germinal products is a sibling set of live-animals in the animals frontend. Reference lists never wait on MDM integration; address search waits on the address lookup becoming a real feature.

claims.statement: INS keeps one aggregated read-model document per notification in the trade-imports-ins-backend notifications collection, with the id Imports.Notification.GBN-AG.<reference number>.
claims.quote: const aggregateIdFor = (referenceNumber: string): string => `Imports.Notification.GBN-AG.${referenceNumber}`;
claims.note: Asserted against Mongo by the spec; the test passed in trace 28659.

claims.statement: The aggregated document exists as soon as the notification is created (a NOTIFICATION_CREATED event fires at creation, before transport details are filled in), with status DRAFT.
claims.quote: NOTIFICATION_CREATED fires immediately at creation (before transport details are filled in), so we poll for the specific fully-populated state rather than bare status=DRAFT.

claims.statement: Before submission the aggregated document reflects the edited draft: status DRAFT, the reference number, origin country, commodity Cow, an arrival date in the future, a lastUpdated date and an aggregateVersion above 0.
claims.quote: expect(draftDoc.status).toBe('DRAFT'); expect(draftDoc.originCountry).toBe(defaultJourneyOptions.countryCode.value); expect(draftDoc.commodity).toBe(commodityCodes.cow); expect(draftDoc.arrivalDate.getTime()).toBeGreaterThan(Date.now()); expect(draftDoc.lastUpdated).toBeInstanceOf(Date); expect(draftDoc.aggregateVersion).toBeGreaterThan(0);
claims.note: The journey posted countryOfOrigin=FR and arrivalDateAtPort=7/11/2026 (trace 28659), so originCountry is the country code.

claims.statement: The aggregated document's commodity is the common name Cow, resolved from the Bos taurus species the user picked.
claims.quote: species=Cow|1148346

claims.statement: Submitting updates the same aggregated document to SUBMITTED rather than creating a second one: exactly one document exists for the notification.
claims.quote: Then — same document is updated to SUBMITTED (no duplicate created) ... expect(await collection.countDocuments({ _id: aggregateId })).toBe(1);

claims.statement: After submission the aggregated document keeps the reference, origin country, commodity, future arrival date and a lastUpdated date, and its aggregateVersion is higher than the draft's.
claims.quote: expect(submittedDoc.status).toBe('SUBMITTED'); ... expect(submittedDoc.aggregateVersion).toBeGreaterThan(draftVersion);

claims.statement: The aggregated store is updated asynchronously from journey events: it catches up with the journey some time after each change rather than in the same request.
claims.quote: await expect.poll(() => collection.findOne({ _id: aggregateId, status: 'SUBMITTED' }), { timeout: timeouts.long }).not.toBeNull();
claims.note: The spec has to poll with a long timeout, and the INS dashboard still showed DRAFT for three searches after submission (claim trace-e2e-p15-106).
